title: Sunline Retail: Kickstart Sprint Canvas & POC Success Criteria
body:
Objective:
Quickly validate a light-touch conversational assistant for Sunline Retail store operations (in-store associates + store ops team) that can answer inventory/location questions, surface next-best actions for returns, and summarize short shift handoffs. Focus on latency, answer usefulness, and integration cost, not building a full agent.

Executive summary (one-liner):
Run a 3-week tactical POC to prove the end-to-end flow: store assistant query -> Redwood-hosted model -> data connector (S3/Redis index) -> structured response templates, with objective metrics for accuracy, median P95 latency, and operational effort to deploy to 10 stores.

Primary success criteria (must-haves):
- Accuracy: 70%+ correct/usable answers on a 120-sample evaluation set defined by Sunline SMEs (binary usable/not usable by a human associate).
- Latency: P95 end-to-end (associate browser -> Redwood API -> response) <= 450ms for cached queries, <= 900ms for cold queries.
- Cost proxy: estimated per-1000-requests inference spend <= $25 (hosted pricing simulation using Redwood Optimize recommendations).
- Integration effort: functional prototype integrated with Sunline's product-catalog index and returns workflow within 3 weeks; handoff docs and runbook created.

Stretch success criteria (nice-to-haves):
- 80%+ usable answers on evaluation set.
- Demo flow includes fallback to human chat handoff with structured logging.
- Basic A/B test plan defined for Dedicated vs Hosted variants.

Non-goals (explicitly out):
- Do NOT build a replacement POS or full agent orchestration.
- No PII extraction or HIPAA-like processing. If any customer PII appears in test data, treat as redacted.

Stakeholders & roles:
- Sunline Product Owner: Mina Alvarez (primary business contact)
- Sunline Technical Lead: Rajesh Iyer (integration owner)
- Redwood SE: Priya Nair (POC lead)
- Redwood Applied ML: Ethan Patel (model/latency advisor)
- Redwood Solutions: Marisol Gomez (on-site workshop facilitator)
- Customer Success: Liam O'Rourke (activation + commercial follow-up)

Timeline (3-week sprint cadence):
Week 0 (prep, 3 business days): kick-off, access, data snapshot transfer, initial eval set lock, infra provisioning.
Week 1: integration baseline — index product catalog snapshot, basic Redwood API calls, seed prompts, latency profiling.
Week 2: iterate prompt templates, add prefix caching and KV-cache tweaks, run 120-sample eval, instrument metrics.
Week 3: user validation sessions with 3 pilot stores, produce runbooks, acceptance sign-off and handoff package.

Key technical assumptions & prerequisites:
- Sunline will provide a sanitized product-catalog export (CSV + images metadata) and a sample of 500 live store queries (anonymized) by Day 1.
- SSH access or an S3 bucket for snapshot ingestion; a read-only Redis instance is optional for live lookups.
- Network: Sunline accepts outbound to Redwood API endpoints from their staging network (allowlist provided).
- We will use Redwood-hosted models for the POC; Dedicated trial is possible for latency comparison if requested.

Acceptance tests (concrete checks we will run for sign-off):
1) Functional correctness: reviewer panel (Sunline ops + 2 store associates) will mark each of 120 eval responses as usable/unusable. Pass if >=70% usable.
2) Latency: run a synthetic load that mimics store UI calls (mix cached & cold). Measure P95; must meet thresholds listed above.
3) Reliability: 48-hour continuous smoke run with 95% success (no errors or 5xx).
4) Integration sanity: product lookup latency <= 120ms (catalog lookup + response assembly).

Data & privacy controls:
- Use redaction scripts on provided query corpus to remove names and phone numbers.
- No long-term storage of Sunline's raw test queries in Redwood demo accounts; ephemeral storage policy documented in runbook.
- KMS usage: for any artifact with store PII, we will use customer-managed keys (if requested).

Observability & metrics (what we'll track):
- Per-request: request id, model variant, token usage, latency (client->server, server processing, model generation), success flag.
- Dashboards: per-route P95 latency, error rate, token cost by route.
- Quality: rolling window usable-rate on evaluation set and pilot user feedback.

Minimum deliverables (end of POC):
- Running prototype accessible to pilot stores (demo URL + credentials).
- Eval report: confusion cases, accuracy numbers, sample transcripts.
- Runbook & deployment checklist (onboarding steps, infra, allowlists).
- Handoff pack: recommended configuration for Dedicated vs Hosted, preliminary cost estimate, next-phase roadmap.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Provided query corpus is too small or high-signal/synthetic -> Mitigation: create synthetic paraphrases and extend eval with store associate sessions.
- Risk: Network allowlist delays -> Mitigation: run a local tunnel fallback and scheduled on-site workshop to establish connectivity.
- Risk: Data contains PII unexpectedly -> Mitigation: stop ingestion, run redaction, escalate to CS/legal.

Workshop agenda (day-of-kickoff, 90 minutes):
- 0-10m: Intros, objectives, confirm success criteria (Priya + Mina)
- 10-25m: Sunline ops demo: typical queries and pain points (Mina + Rajesh)
- 25-45m: Technical architecture walkthrough (Redwood) — data flow, auth, integration points (Ethan)
- 45-60m: Live ingestion test (engineer pairing) — confirm sample index ingestion
- 60-75m: Evaluation plan & handoff criteria (Marisol)
- 75-90m: Action items, owners, and calendar next steps

Unresolved questions (to capture during kickoff):
- Will Sunline allow 3rd-party cookies/CSRF tokens for the staging UI demo?
- Which fields (SKU, aisle, image_url) are authoritative in their catalog?
- Who is the final approver for POC acceptance (title + email)?

Action items (post-kickoff immediate):
- Priya: Create skeleton runbook + populate with initial infra steps (Due: Day 1)
- Rajesh: Provide sanitized catalog CSV and 500-sample query log (Due: Day 1)
- Ethan: Prepare Redwood Optimize baseline simulation and predicted cost matrix (Due: Day 3)
- Marisol: Schedule pilot-store sessions and recruit 3 associates for user testing (Due: Day 7)

Notes to self / team shorthand (working-doc style):
- Try prefix caching on frequent SKU queries — big win for P95.
- Keep prompts short to reduce token cost; prefer structured response templates.
- If latency > target on cold queries, spin a Dedicated trial node for comparison (cheap A/B).
- Prepare quick fallback template to human chat with context package to speed handoff.

Acceptance review meeting (scheduled):
- Date: 2025-03-03, 14:00 PT -> confirm calendar once pilot-store sessions complete.

Handoff criteria (if passed):
- All core success criteria met OR business sponsor signs off on go/no-go with mitigation plan for any missing metric.
- Handoff docs uploaded to Confluence ID CONFLUENCE-POC-SUNLINE-001 and GitHub template repo forked for their infra.

Appendix: quick eval rubric (for reviewers):
- 0 = wrong/confusing; requires corrective steps from associate
- 1 = partial; correct but missing key action (associate may need to ask follow-up)
- 2 = usable; clears the issue or gives a next-best-action that associate can execute

End of doc — working draft.
Comments: prefer lightweight artifacts for Sunline (they want fast wins). Keep this doc living during week 0; will move to final playbook if POC passes.
